title: Telemetry inventory crashes on malformed gate-attempts rows instead of completing the scan

finding.claim: Telemetry inventory crashes on malformed gate-attempts rows instead of completing the scan
finding.recommendation: Parse gate-attempts.jsonl defensively: use a with-open block, skip blank lines, and catch JSONDecodeError per line so one malformed row does not abort the entire scan. If malformed rows should fail the probe, emit a controlled finding in the output instead of raising.

refutation.reason: The code explicitly filters out blank lines before parsing, using the condition `if ln.strip()`, which prevents JSONDecodeError from malformed or empty rows from aborting the scan.

probe.summary: Records-scan probe (`probes/closing_records_scan_probe.py`, section b): the scan was run in a synthetic tree whose gate-attempts.jsonl carries [valid, blank, MALFORMED non-blank, valid] rows. Exit code 1 — `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` out of the telemetry block (records_scan.py: `rows = [_json.loads(ln) for ln in open(...) if ln.strip()]`), and no result file was written: the scan aborts instead of completing. The blank-line filter the refutation cites works — for blank lines; a non-blank malformed row is the unhandled shape.
